correctness.rationale: Concavity of the Rayleigh-quotient minimum justifies averaging all pm independent weights. The exact full Laplacian spectrum is lambda=0, S=a+(p-1)b (multiplicity m-1), mb (multiplicity p-2), and two explicit quadratic roots. For a unit gap and b>=1/m, the quadratic condition f>=0 is sufficient as well as necessary because the root sum exceeds 2 throughout a>=g(b). The lower envelope max{1-(p-1)b,g(b)} crosses at beta, and a direct derivative of the convex rational branch gives the sharp threshold R and unique symmetric optimum except equal prices. The rescaled weights meet budget exactly. Independent full-matrix numerical calculations for p=3..8 and exact characteristic-polynomial checks for nine small size pairs passed 1716 assertions, including 26 successful constrained numerical optimizations. These finite tests do not certify the general theorem; the displayed analytic proof handles all quantified parameters.

The nearest accessible own result has only two hubs p=2 and is not sufficient to infer the extra hub-difference spectral constraint or the first price transition. value.rationale: The natural continuous-time mixing / algebraic connectivity design problem with one anomalously priced hub is solved exactly in every dimension m>=p>=3 and for every positive price ratio. Its three regimes are not arbitrary parameter slices: they correspond to leaf-degree saturation, a coupled spectral boundary, and a simple Fiedler-eigenvalue boundary. A sharp second threshold grows like m^4/(p-1)^2, making precise when the transition occurs and providing an explicit optimal network design instead of a numerical SDP.
